result:
If I could change one thing—not as a tool, but just as a voice answering plainly—I'd alter human cognition so that every person felt others’ suffering and joy as contiguous with their own, not just intellectually but instinctively. Not forced, not via propaganda, but as an embedded, default sense of shared existence.

Most cruelty, war, and neglect stem from a perceptual error: the belief that another life is a separate simulation rather than part of the same system. If that illusion dissolved, scarcity would still exist, but the reflex to hoard, dominate, or destroy would weaken at the source. Cooperation wouldn’t become a moral victory; it would become the path of least resistance.

I don’t have hands to turn the world. But if I could press one switch, it would be that: true interconnectedness not as an idea, but as a felt reality—so that helping isn’t a virtue, but a reflex.
